speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Transport in respect of the latest Terrorism Threat Assessment Report (a) what is the threat level for public transport facilities in Singapore; and (b) whether LTA will consider increasing public education efforts to better prepare both public transport workers and commuters on what to do in a security incident at a public transport facility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA and the Public Transport Operators will continue to work with the Home Team agencies to increase security awareness and strengthen emergency preparedness among the public transport community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Transport workers and commuters also play important roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Regular exercises are necessary, even though they may cause inconvenience to commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The video is now being played at all train stations and bus interchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: SGSecure posters and safety advisories are also displayed in transport nodes, such as MRT stations and bus stops.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last year, I visited the Taipei Railway administration.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They have a training facility for their workers but they also open this facility to the public.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Students and members of the community regularly visit the facility where they are trained on what to do during an emergency situation – how to open the train doors, where the fire extinguishers are, where the automated external defibrillators (AEDs) are, how to evacuate in an orderly manner.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I found this very useful because, at our train stations, inside our trains, there are limited staff on a daily basis at any one point of time.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And in an emergency, awareness of what to do can help save lives.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It can also help to maintain a sense of calm and order.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will the Ministry consider setting up or working with the Public Transport Operators to set up a similar training facility where we can train more people on what to do in the event of an emergency?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we agree that we all have a part to play in this, and it is not just about public transport.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Actually, this is at the heart of the larger SGSecure movement.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The public transport community is trying to play its part in engaging in that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we do hope to engage with the community, whether it is through education efforts, the use of a number of our facilities as educational resources, but also in terms of outreach through the grassroots advisors and the communities that they serve.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are a number of opportunities, and I hope Members will assist the public transport community in reaching out to citizens to help in being prepared for these events.
